ideas.title: Static from my own feathers
ideas.critique: Charge, induced forces and a spark whose path comes from solved geometry are physics the island has never had, and a friend's nose getting zapped is a moment people would share. But triboelectric charging is noisy in reality, so the 'how long and with what you rub' table will likely become a typed-in rate. It also sits on a branch beside the road's magnets, coils and cells, not on it.

ideas.title: Lightning makes magnet stones
ideas.critique: Giving the magnet stone a cause the player can bring about is a clever origin, and choosing the strike point from field enhancement is real. But the play is: place pegs, wait for a storm, then walk round with the compass bowl the island has already posted, so the payoff is a needle twitching after an event you never see work. A single strike's Biot-Savart pulse through one coercivity threshold is a one-case rig.

ideas.title: The scrap claw: only iron comes up
ideas.critique: This is round 1's scrap crane again, with mixed materials and a claw-machine frame added. The frame is the obvious game to build from a lifting magnet, and the materials table deciding what answers is the one real addition. It only escapes being a repeat of the empty coil post if pegs that lie tangled and the stuck shell actually come out of contact, not out of a staged heap.

ideas.title: Crank it and the wire glows
ideas.nearest: A wire that spins by itself
ideas.critique: Induction from flux through every wound turn, with the load felt back on the crank, is a real new solver piece, and feeling it in your hands is the strong part. Honestly computed, though, a hand-turned lodestone past a beach-wound coil will barely warm a wire, so 'glows' is where the numbers will get bent. Without the glow the toy is a crank that gets slightly heavier.
